## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this 

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
  
```{r}
# Load tidyverse and palmerpenguins libraries
  
```
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
```
```{r}
# Create a ggplot scatter plot using the penguins dataset.
# Plot bill_length_mm on the x-axis and bill_depth_mm on the y-axis.
# Color points by species and use geom_point with size 3.
# Add a minimal theme and clean labels.
ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm, color = species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Bill Length vs Bill Depth in Penguins",
    x = "Bill Length (mm)",
    y = "Bill Depth (mm)",
    color = "Species"
  )
```
```{r}
# Create a boxplot using the penguins dataset.
# Compare flipper_length_mm across different species.
# Facet the plot by island.
# Use a custom colour palette and theme_minimal().
ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm, fill = species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ island) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Flipper Length Distribution by Species and Island",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Flipper Length (mm)",
    fill = "Species"
  )
```

```{r}
sst <- 30.2

if (sst > 29.5) {
  print("Warning: Marine heatwave threshold exceeded!")
} else {
  print("SST remains within baseline parameters.")
}
```
```{r}
coral_monitoring <- tibble(
  site = c("Site_A", "Site_B", "Site_C"),
  depth_m = c(12, 35, 8)
)

coral_monitoring <- coral_monitoring %>%
  mutate(
    zone = if_else(depth_m > 30, "Deep Reef", "Shallow Reef")
  )

print(coral_monitoring)
```
```{r}
coral_monitoring <- coral_monitoring %>%
  mutate(
    zone = case_when(
      depth_m < 10 ~ "Lagoon/Flats",
      depth_m <= 30 ~ "Crest/Slope",
      depth_m > 30 ~ "Mesophotic/Deep",
      TRUE ~ "Unclassified"
    )
  )

print(coral_monitoring)
```
```{r}
marine_stations <- tibble(
  station = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
  salinity = c(35, 28, 32, 12)
)

marine_stations <- marine_stations %>%
  mutate(
    environment_type = case_when(
      salinity < 15 ~ "Estuarine",
      salinity <= 30 ~ "Brackish",
      salinity > 30 ~ "Marine"
    )
  )

print(marine_stations)
```
'''
## Understanding the Code

**What does mutate() do?**

The mutate() function creates or modifies columns in a dataset.

**What does %>% do?**

The pipe operator passes the result of one operation to the next function.

**How can we access help?**

Type `?dplyr::mutate` in the RStudio Console to access documentation.

```{r}
calculate_coral_mortality <- function(initial_count, surviving_count) {
  if (initial_count <= 0) {
    stop("Initial count must be greater than zero.")
  }

  mortality <- (initial_count - surviving_count) / initial_count
  return(mortality)
}

calculate_coral_mortality(120, 84)
```
```{r}
convert_temp_c_to_f <- function(temp_c) {
  if (temp_c < -273.15) {
    stop("Temperature cannot be below absolute zero.")
  }

  temp_f <- (temp_c * 9/5) + 32
  return(temp_f)
}

convert_temp_c_to_f(25)
```
```{r}
#| error: true
convert_temp_c_to_f(-300)
```
